import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')

# ============ SECTION 3: Topic & MeSH Analysis ============
print("=== SECTION 3: Topic & MeSH Analysis ===")

# Major topics
topics = df[df['major_topic'] != '']['major_topic'].value_counts().head(30)
print("Top 30 major topics:")
for t, c in topics.items():
    print(f"  {t}: {c}")

# Topics by year
print("\nTop 10 topics by year:")
topic_year = df[df['major_topic'] != ''].groupby(['pub_year', 'major_topic']).size().reset_index(name='count')
for year in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    ty = topic_year[topic_year['pub_year'] == year].nlargest(10, 'count')
    print(f"\n  {year}:")
    for _, r in ty.iterrows():
        print(f"    {r['major_topic']}: {r['count']}")

# Keywords
keywords_all = df[df['keywords'] != '']['keywords']
all_kw = []
for kw in keywords_all:
    all_kw.extend([k.strip() for k in str(kw).split(';')])
kw_counter = Counter(all_kw)
print("\nTop 30 keywords:")
for kw, c in kw_counter.most_common(30):
    print(f"  {kw}: {c}")

# Keywords by year
print("\nKeywords year comparison:")
for year in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    kw_year = df[df['pub_year'] == year]
    kw_all_year = []
    for kw in kw_year[kw_year['keywords'] != '']['keywords']:
        kw_all_year.extend([k.strip() for k in str(kw).split(';')])
    kw_counter_year = Counter(kw_all_year)
    top_kw = kw_counter_year.most_common(15)
    print(f"\n  {year} top keywords:")
    for kw, c in top_kw:
        print(f"    {kw}: {c}")

# ============ SECTION 4: Open Access ============
print("\n=== SECTION 4: Open Access ===")
oa_yearly = df.groupby('pub_year')['open_access'].agg(['sum', 'count', 'mean'])
print("OA by year:")
print(oa_yearly)

# OA monthly
df_km = df[df['pub_month_num'] != 0].copy()
df_km['year_month'] = df_km['pub_year'].astype(str) + '-' + df_km['pub_month_num'].astype(str).str.zfill(2)
oa_monthly = df_km.groupby('year_month')['open_access'].agg(['sum', 'count', 'mean']).sort_index()
print("\nOA monthly:")
print(oa_monthly.to_string())

# OA by research type
print("\nOA by research type (top categories):")
# Parse primary research type
def get_primary_type(rt):
    if pd.isna(rt) or rt == '':
        return 'Unknown'
    types = [t.strip() for t in str(rt).split(';')]
    # Check for specific types
    for t in ['Systematic Review', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Preprint', 'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Journal Article']:
        if t in types:
            return t
    return types[0]

df['primary_type'] = df['research_type'].apply(get_primary_type)
oa_by_type = df.groupby('primary_type')['open_access'].agg(['sum', 'count', 'mean'])
print(oa_by_type.sort_values('count', ascending=False).to_string())

python3 << 'PYEOF'
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')

# ============ SECTION 5: Research Type & Collaboration ============
print("=== SECTION 5: Research Type & Collaboration ===")

# Parse research types
def get_primary_type(rt):
    if pd.isna(rt) or rt == '':
        return 'Unknown'
    types = [t.strip() for t in str(rt).split(';')]
    for t in ['Systematic Review', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Preprint', 'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Journal Article']:
        if t in types:
            return t
    return types[0]

df['primary_type'] = df['research_type'].apply(get_primary_type)
print("Primary research type distribution:")
rt_counts = df['primary_type'].value_counts()
for t, c in rt_counts.items():
    print(f"  {t}: {c} ({c/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")

# Authors by type
print("\nMedian authors by research type:")
for t in rt_counts.head(7).index:
    subset = df[df['primary_type'] == t]
    print(f"  {t}: median={subset['authors_count'].median():.0f}, mean={subset['authors_count'].mean():.1f}, max={subset['authors_count'].max()}")

# Authors by country
print("\nMedian authors by top countries:")
country_fix = {
    'United States': 'USA',
    'PR China': 'China',
    "People's Republic of China": 'China',
    'Republic of Korea': 'South Korea',
}
df['country_clean'] = df['country'].replace(country_fix)
top_countries = df['country_clean'].value_counts().head(15).index
for c in top_countries:
    subset = df[df['country_clean'] == c]
    print(f"  {c}: median={subset['authors_count'].median():.0f}, mean={subset['authors_count'].mean():.1f}")

# Authors over time
print("\nMedian authors by year:")
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    subset = df[df['pub_year'] == y]
    print(f"  {y}: median={subset['authors_count'].median():.0f}, mean={subset['authors_count'].mean():.1f}")

# Research type by year
print("\nResearch type distribution by year:")
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    subset = df[df['pub_year'] == y]
    rt_year = subset['primary_type'].value_counts()
    print(f"\n  {y}:")
    for t, c in rt_year.items():
        print(f"    {t}: {c} ({c/len(subset)*100:.1f}%)")

# Abstract words
print("\nAbstract words stats:")
print(df['abstract_words'].describe())
print("\nMedian abstract words by year:")
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    subset = df[df['pub_year'] == y]
    print(f"  {y}: median={subset['abstract_words'].median():.0f}, mean={subset['abstract_words'].mean():.1f}")

# Authors distribution buckets
print("\nAuthors count distribution:")
bins = [0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20, 50, 200]
df['author_bucket'] = pd.cut(df['authors_count'], bins=bins, right=True)
print(df['author_bucket'].value_counts().sort_index())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the Biomedical Research Landscape 2024-2026 HTML report with embedded charts."""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
import seaborn as sns
from collections import Counter
import base64
import io
import json
from datetime import datetime

# ---------- Style ----------
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.labelsize': 12,
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'savefig.dpi': 150,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.1,
})

PALETTE = ['#1b4f72', '#2e86c1', '#3498db', '#85c1e9', '#d4e6f1',
           '#117a65', '#1abc9c', '#a3e4d7', '#d5f5e3', '#f9e79f',
           '#b03a2e', '#e74c3c', '#f1948a', '#fadbd8', '#7d3c98']
ACCENT = '#e74c3c'
BLUE1 = '#1b4f72'
BLUE2 = '#2e86c1'
GREEN1 = '#117a65'
ORANGE1 = '#d35400'

def fig_to_b64(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode()
    plt.close(fig)
    return f'data:image/png;base64,{b64}'

# ---------- Load Data ----------
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')
df['pub_date'] = pd.to_datetime(
    df['pub_year'].astype(str) + '-' + df['pub_month_num'].astype(str).replace('0', '01') + '-01',
    errors='coerce'
)

# Normalize countries
country_fix = {
    'United States': 'USA', 'United States of America': 'USA',
    'PR China': 'China', "People's Republic of China": 'China',
    'Republic of Korea': 'South Korea', 'P R China': 'China',
}
df['country_clean'] = df['country'].replace(country_fix)

# Parse research type
def get_primary_type(rt):
    if pd.isna(rt) or rt == '':
        return 'Other'
    types = [t.strip() for t in str(rt).split(';')]
    for t in ['Systematic Review', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Preprint',
              'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Editorial', 'Letter', 'Journal Article']:
        if t in types:
            return t
    return types[0] if types else 'Other'

df['primary_type'] = df['research_type'].apply(get_primary_type)

# Sort month-year
month_order = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec']
df['month_order'] = df['pub_month'].apply(lambda x: month_order.index(x) if x in month_order else 99)

charts = {}

# ==================== CHART 1: Monthly Publication Volume ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5.5))
monthly_data = []
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    for m_idx, m_name in enumerate(month_order):
        cnt = len(df[(df['pub_year'] == y) & (df['pub_month'] == m_name)])
        if cnt > 0 or not (y == 2026 and m_idx > 2):
            monthly_data.append({'label': f"{m_name}-{y}", 'year': y, 'month_idx': m_idx, 'count': cnt})

md = pd.DataFrame(monthly_data)

colors_by_year = {2024: BLUE1, 2025: BLUE2, 2026: GREEN1}
bar_colors = [colors_by_year.get(y, '#999') for y in md['year']]

bars = ax.bar(range(len(md)), md['count'], color=bar_colors, width=0.75, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)

# Add year separators
prev_year = None
for i, y in enumerate(md['year']):
    if y != prev_year:
        ax.axvline(x=i - 0.5, color='#ccc', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
        prev_year = y

ax.set_xticks(range(len(md)))
ax.set_xticklabels(md['label'], rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=7)
ax.set_ylabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Monthly Biomedical Publication Volume (Jan 2024 – Mar 2026)', fontweight='bold', pad=15)

from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=BLUE1, label='2024'),
                   Patch(facecolor=BLUE2, label='2025'),
                   Patch(facecolor=GREEN1, label='2026')]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(md['count']) * 1.15)

# Annotate peaks
top3 = md.nlargest(3, 'count')
for _, r in top3.iterrows():
    idx = md[md['label'] == r['label']].index[0]
    ax.annotate(f"{int(r['count'])}", (idx, r['count']), textcoords="offset points",
                xytext=(0, 6), ha='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=BLUE1)

# Add note about indexing skew
ax.text(0.99, 0.95, 'Note: 2024 dominance reflects PubMed indexing lag;\n2025-2026 records still accumulating.',
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8, ha='right', va='top',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='#fff3cd', alpha=0.8))

charts['monthly_volume'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 2: Yearly Volume + OA ====================
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.5))

# Yearly volume
yearly = df.groupby('pub_year').size()
years = [2024, 2025, 2026]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the Biomedical Research Landscape 2024-2026 HTML report with embedded charts."""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
import seaborn as sns
from collections import Counter
import base64
import io
import json
from datetime import datetime

# ---------- Style ----------
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.labelsize': 12,
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'savefig.dpi': 150,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.1,
})

PALETTE = ['#1b4f72', '#2e86c1', '#3498db', '#85c1e9', '#d4e6f1',
           '#117a65', '#1abc9c', '#a3e4d7', '#d5f5e3', '#f9e79f',
           '#b03a2e', '#e74c3c', '#f1948a', '#fadbd8', '#7d3c98']
ACCENT = '#e74c3c'
BLUE1 = '#1b4f72'
BLUE2 = '#2e86c1'
GREEN1 = '#117a65'
ORANGE1 = '#d35400'

def fig_to_b64(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode()
    plt.close(fig)
    return f'data:image/png;base64,{b64}'

# ---------- Load Data ----------
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')
df['pub_date'] = pd.to_datetime(
    df['pub_year'].astype(str) + '-' + df['pub_month_num'].astype(str).replace('0', '01') + '-01',
    errors='coerce'
)

# Normalize countries
country_fix = {
    'United States': 'USA', 'United States of America': 'USA',
    'PR China': 'China', "People's Republic of China": 'China',
    'Republic of Korea': 'South Korea', 'P R China': 'China',
}
df['country_clean'] = df['country'].replace(country_fix)

# Parse research type
def get_primary_type(rt):
    if pd.isna(rt) or rt == '':
        return 'Other'
    types = [t.strip() for t in str(rt).split(';')]
    for t in ['Systematic Review', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Preprint',
              'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Editorial', 'Letter', 'Journal Article']:
        if t in types:
            return t
    return types[0] if types else 'Other'

df['primary_type'] = df['research_type'].apply(get_primary_type)

# Sort month-year
month_order = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec']
df['month_order'] = df['pub_month'].apply(lambda x: month_order.index(x) if x in month_order else 99)

charts = {}

# ==================== CHART 1: Monthly Publication Volume ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5.5))
monthly_data = []
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    for m_idx, m_name in enumerate(month_order):
        cnt = len(df[(df['pub_year'] == y) & (df['pub_month'] == m_name)])
        if cnt > 0 or not (y == 2026 and m_idx > 2):
            monthly_data.append({'label': f"{m_name}-{y}", 'year': y, 'month_idx': m_idx, 'count': cnt})

md = pd.DataFrame(monthly_data)

colors_by_year = {2024: BLUE1, 2025: BLUE2, 2026: GREEN1}
bar_colors = [colors_by_year.get(y, '#999') for y in md['year']]

bars = ax.bar(range(len(md)), md['count'], color=bar_colors, width=0.75, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)

# Add year separators
prev_year = None
for i, y in enumerate(md['year']):
    if y != prev_year:
        ax.axvline(x=i - 0.5, color='#ccc', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
        prev_year = y

ax.set_xticks(range(len(md)))
ax.set_xticklabels(md['label'], rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=7)
ax.set_ylabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Monthly Biomedical Publication Volume (Jan 2024 – Mar 2026)', fontweight='bold', pad=15)

from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=BLUE1, label='2024'),
                   Patch(facecolor=BLUE2, label='2025'),
                   Patch(facecolor=GREEN1, label='2026')]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(md['count']) * 1.15)

# Annotate peaks
top3 = md.nlargest(3, 'count')
for _, r in top3.iterrows():
    idx = md[md['label'] == r['label']].index[0]
    ax.annotate(f"{int(r['count'])}", (idx, r['count']), textcoords="offset points",
                xytext=(0, 6), ha='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=BLUE1)

# Add note about indexing skew
ax.text(0.99, 0.95, 'Note: 2024 dominance reflects PubMed indexing lag;\n2025-2026 records still accumulating.',
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8, ha='right', va='top',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='#fff3cd', alpha=0.8))

charts['monthly_volume'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 2: Yearly Volume + OA ====================
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.5))

# Yearly volume
yearly = df.groupby('pub_year').size()
years = [2024, 2025, 2026]
counts = [yearly.get(y, 0) for y in years]
colors_yr = [BLUE1, BLUE2, GREEN1]
bars = ax1.bar(years, counts, color=colors_yr, width=0.6, edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)
for bar, c in zip(bars, counts):
    ax1.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 30, f'{c:,}',
             ha='center', fontweight='bold', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_ylabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Total Publications by Year', fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xticks(years)

# OA rate over time
oa_yearly = df.groupby('pub_year')['open_access'].mean() * 100
oa_rates = [oa_yearly.get(y, 0) for y in years]
ax2.plot(years, oa_rates, 'o-', color=ORANGE1, linewidth=2.5, markersize=10, markerfacecolor='white',
         markeredgewidth=2)
for y, r in zip(years, oa_rates):
    ax2.annotate(f'{r:.1f}%', (y, r), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 12),
                 ha='center', fontweight='bold', fontsize=11, color=ORANGE1)
ax2.set_ylabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold', color=ORANGE1)
ax2.set_title('Open Access Rate by Year', fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xticks(years)
ax2.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax2.axhline(y=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color='#999', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.6)
ax2.text(2025.5, df['open_access'].mean() * 100 + 1, f'Overall: {df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%',
         fontsize=8, color='#999', ha='right')

fig.tight_layout()
charts['yearly_oa'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 3: OA Monthly Trend ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
df_km = df[df['pub_month_num'] != 0].copy()
df_km['ym_label'] = df_km['pub_month'].astype(str) + '-' + df_km['pub_year'].astype(str)
oa_monthly = df_km.groupby('ym_label')['open_access'].agg(['mean', 'count']).reset_index()
oa_monthly['mean'] = oa_monthly['mean'] * 100

# Sort
monthly_labels = []
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    for m in month_order:
        label = f"{m}-{y}"
        if label in oa_monthly['ym_label'].values:
            monthly_labels.append(label)

oa_monthly['sort_key'] = oa_monthly['ym_label'].apply(
    lambda x: monthly_labels.index(x) if x in monthly_labels else 999)
oa_monthly = oa_monthly.sort_values('sort_key')

# Color by year
bar_colors = []
for _, r in oa_monthly.iterrows():
    yr = int(r['ym_label'].split('-')[1])
    bar_colors.append({2024: BLUE1, 2025: BLUE2, 2026: GREEN1}.get(yr, '#999'))

ax.bar(range(len(oa_monthly)), oa_monthly['mean'], color=bar_colors, width=0.7, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)
ax.axhline(y=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color=ORANGE1, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.7,
           label=f'Overall ({df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%)')
ax.set_xticks(range(len(oa_monthly)))
ax.set_xticklabels(oa_monthly['ym_label'], rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=7)
ax.set_ylabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Monthly Open Access Rate', fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(loc='lower left', fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylim(0, 105)

# Add trend line
xs = range(len(oa_monthly))
z = np.polyfit(xs, oa_monthly['mean'].values, 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)
ax.plot(xs, p(xs), color=ORANGE1, linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.5, linestyle='-')

charts['oa_monthly'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 4: Geographic Distribution ====================
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5.5))

top15 = df['country_clean'].value_counts().head(15)
colors_geo = [BLUE1 if i < 5 else BLUE2 if i < 10 else '#85c1e9' for i in range(len(top15))]
ax1.barh(range(len(top15)-1, -1, -1), top15.values, color=colors_geo[::-1], height=0.7, edgecolor='white')
ax1.set_yticks(range(len(top15)-1, -1, -1))
ax1.set_yticklabels(top15.index[::-1], fontsize=9)
ax1.set_xlabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Top 15 Countries by Publication Count', fontweight='bold')
for i, (val, name) in enumerate(zip(top15.values[::-1], top15.index[::-1])):
    ax1.text(val + 3, i, str(val), va='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=BLUE1)

# Top 5 country share over time
top5_countries = ['China', 'USA', 'India', 'Japan', 'Canada']
year_country_data = {}
for y in years:
    y_df = df[df['pub_year'] == y]
    total = len(y_df)
    year_country_data[y] = {}
    for c in top5_countries:
        year_country_data[y][c] = len(y_df[y_df['country_clean'] == c]) / total * 100

x = np.arange(len(years))
width = 0.15
for i, country in enumerate(top5_countries):
    vals = [year_country_data[y].get(country, 0) for y in years]
    ax2.bar(x + i * width, vals, width, label=country, color=PALETTE[i], edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)

ax2.set_ylabel('Share of Publications (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Top 5 Countries: Share Over Time', fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xticks(x + width * 2)
ax2.set_xticklabels(years)
ax2.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)

fig.tight_layout()
charts['geography'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 5: OA by Country ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
top12 = df['country_clean'].value_counts().head(12).index
oa_by_country = []
for c in top12:
    subset = df[df['country_clean'] == c]
    oa_by_country.append({'country': c, 'oa_rate': subset['open_access'].mean() * 100, 'count': len(subset)})
oa_df = pd.DataFrame(oa_by_country).sort_values('oa_rate', ascending=True)

colors_oa_cty = [BLUE2 if r < df['open_access'].mean() * 100 else GREEN1 for r in oa_df['oa_rate']]
ax.barh(range(len(oa_df)), oa_df['oa_rate'], color=colors_oa_cty, height=0.6, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(oa_df)))
ax.set_yticklabels(oa_df['country'], fontsize=10)
ax.set_xlabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Open Access Rate by Top Countries', fontweight='bold')
ax.axvline(x=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color=ORANGE1, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5,
           label=f'Overall ({df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%)')
ax.legend(loc='lower right', fontsize=9)
for i, (val, cnt) in enumerate(zip(oa_df['oa_rate'], oa_df['count'])):
    ax.text(val + 0.5, i, f'{val:.1f}% (n={cnt})', va='center', fontsize=8, color='#333')

charts['oa_country'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 6: Major Topics ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
top_topics = df[df['major_topic'] != '']['major_topic'].value_counts().head(20)
colors_topic = [BLUE1 if i < 5 else BLUE2 if i < 10 else '#85c1e9' for i in range(len(top_topics))]
ax.barh(range(len(top_topics)-1, -1, -1), top_topics.values, color=colors_topic[::-1], height=0.7, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top_topics)-1, -1, -1))
ax.set_yticklabels(top_topics.index[::-1], fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Top 20 Major MeSH Topics', fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(top_topics.values[::-1]):
    ax.text(v + 0.2, i, str(v), va='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=BLUE1)

charts['topics'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 7: Topic Trends ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
# Focus on top topics that appear across years
trend_topics = ['COVID-19', 'Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2', 'Breast Neoplasms',
                'Gastrointestinal Microbiome', 'Alzheimer Disease', 'MicroRNAs',
                'Quality of Life', 'Neoplasms']
trend_data = []
for topic in trend_topics:
    for y in years:
        cnt = len(df[(df['pub_year'] == y) & (df['major_topic'] == topic)])
        trend_data.append({'topic': topic, 'year': y, 'count': cnt})
td = pd.DataFrame(trend_data)

for i, topic in enumerate(trend_topics):
    t_sub = td[td['topic'] == topic]
    ax.plot(t_sub['year'], t_sub['count'], 'o-', color=PALETTE[i], linewidth=2, markersize=6, label=topic)

ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Major Topic Publication Trends (2024–2026)', fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2, loc='upper right')
ax.set_xticks(years)

charts['topic_trends'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 8: Keywords Word Cloud Alternative (Top Keywords) ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
# Get top keywords excluding generic ones
generic_kw = {'Humans', 'Female', 'Male', 'Animals', 'Adult', 'Middle Aged', 'Aged', 'nan',
              'Child', 'Adolescent', 'Young Adult', 'Child, Preschool', 'Infant', 'Infant, Newborn'}
all_kw = []
for kw in df[df['keywords'] != '']['keywords']:
    all_kw.extend([k.strip() for k in str(kw).split(';')])
kw_counter = Counter(all_kw)
top_kw_disease = [(kw, cnt) for kw, cnt in kw_counter.most_common(100) if kw not in generic_kw][:25]

labels_kw = [k for k, _ in top_kw_disease]
values_kw = [v for _, v in top_kw_disease]
colors_kw = [BLUE1 if i < 8 else BLUE2 if i < 16 else '#85c1e9' for i in range(len(labels_kw))]

ax.barh(range(len(labels_kw)-1, -1, -1), values_kw, color=colors_kw[::-1], height=0.7, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(labels_kw)-1, -1, -1))
ax.set_yticklabels(labels_kw[::-1], fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel('Occurrences', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Top 25 Domain-Specific MeSH Keywords (Excluding Demographics)', fontweight='bold')

charts['keywords'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 9: Research Type Distribution ====================
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5))

rt_counts = df['primary_type'].value_counts()
explode = [0.03 if c == 'Journal Article' else 0 for c in rt_counts.index]
colors_rt = [BLUE1, BLUE2, GREEN1, '#85c1e9', ORANGE1, '#a3e4d7', '#d5f5e3', '#f9e79f', '#f1948a']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax1.pie(rt_counts.values, labels=rt_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%',
                                    colors=colors_rt[:len(rt_counts)], startangle=140,
                                    textprops={'fontsize': 8}, pctdistance=0.75)
for at in autotexts:
    at.set_fontweight('bold')
ax1.set_title('Research Type Distribution', fontweight='bold')

# Authors by research type
rt_order = ['Journal Article', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Systematic Review',
            'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Preprint']
rt_meds = []
for rt in rt_order:
    subset = df[df['primary_type'] == rt]
    if len(subset) > 0:
        rt_meds.append({'type': rt, 'median': subset['authors_count'].median(), 'count': len(subset)})
rt_meds_df = pd.DataFrame(rt_meds)
ax2.barh(range(len(rt_meds_df)-1, -1, -1), rt_meds_df['median'],

         height=0.6, edgecolor='white')
ax2.set_yticks(range(len(rt_meds_df)-1, -1, -1))
ax2.set_yticklabels(rt_meds_df['type'][::-1], fontsize=9)
ax2.set_xlabel('Median Authors', fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Median Authors per Research Type', fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(rt_meds_df['median'][::-1]):
    ax2.text(v + 0.1, i, f'{v:.0f}', va='center', fontweight='bold', fontsize=9, color=BLUE1)

fig.tight_layout()
charts['research_type'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 10: Author Collaboration ====================
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5))

# Author distribution histogram
ax1.hist(df['authors_count'], bins=50, color=BLUE2, edgecolor='white', alpha=0.85)
ax1.axvline(x=df['authors_count'].median(), color=ORANGE1, linestyle='--', linewidth=2,
            label=f'Median: {df["authors_count"].median():.0f}')

ax1.legend(fontsize=8)

country_meds = []
for c in top10_countries:
    subset = df[df['country_clean'] == c]
    country_meds.append({'country': c, 'median': subset['authors_count'].median(),
                         'mean': subset['authors_count'].mean(), 'count': len(subset)})
cty_df = pd.DataFrame(country_meds).sort_values('median', ascending=True)

ax2.barh(range(len(cty_df)-1, -1, -1), cty_df['median'],
         color=[BLUE2 if i < 7 else '#85c1e9' for i in range(len(cty_df))],
         height=0.6, edgecolor='white')

fig.tight_layout()

# ==================== CHART 11: OA by Research Type ====================

rt_oa_data = []
for rt in ['Journal Article', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Systematic Review',

        rt_oa_data.append({'type': rt, 'oa_rate': subset['open_access'].mean() * 100, 'count': len(subset)})
rt_oa_df = pd.DataFrame(rt_oa_data)

colors_rt_oa = [BLUE2 if r < df['open_access'].mean() * 100 else GREEN1 for r in rt_oa_df['oa_rate']]
ax.bar(range(len(rt_oa_df)), rt_oa_df['oa_rate'], color=colors_rt_oa, width=0.6, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(rt_oa_df)))
ax.set_xticklabels(rt_oa_df['type'], rotation=30, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Open Access Rate by Research Type', fontweight='bold')
ax.axhline(y=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color=ORANGE1, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5,
           label=f'Overall ({df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%)')
ax.legend(fontsize=9)
for i, (v, c) in enumerate(zip(rt_oa_df['oa_rate'], rt_oa_df['count'])):
    ax.text(i, v + 1, f'{v:.1f}%\n(n={c})', ha='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')

charts['oa_research_type'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 12: Emerging Topics - Growth Rate ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.5))
# Calculate topics that appear in 2025/2026 but not heavily in 2024
topic_year_counts = df[df['major_topic'] != ''].groupby(['major_topic', 'pub_year']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
topic_year_counts = topic_year_counts[[2024, 2025, 2026]] if all(y in topic_year_counts.columns for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]) else topic_year_counts

# Growth topics: present in 2025/2026, with positive trajectory
topic_year_counts['growth_25_26'] = topic_year_counts[2026] - topic_year_counts[2025]
topic_year_counts['has_recent'] = (topic_year_counts[2025] > 0) | (topic_year_counts[2026] > 0)
topic_year_counts['increasing'] = topic_year_counts['growth_25_26'] > 0

emerging = topic_year_counts[topic_year_counts['has_recent']].sort_values('growth_25_26', ascending=False).head(15)
labels_em = [f"{t}\n(2024:{int(r[2024])} 2025:{int(r[2025])} 2026:{int(r[2026])})"
             for t, r in emerging.iterrows()]
vals_em = [r['growth_25_26'] for _, r in emerging.iterrows()]
colors_em = [GREEN1 if v > 0 else ORANGE1 for v in vals_em]

ax.barh(range(len(labels_em)-1, -1, -1), vals_em, color=colors_em[::-1], height=0.6, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(labels_em)-1, -1, -1))
ax.set_yticklabels(labels_em[::-1], fontsize=6.5)
ax.set_xlabel('Change in Publication Count (2026 – 2025)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Emerging Topics: Growth in Recent Publications (2025→2026)', fontweight='bold')
ax.axvline(x=0, color='#999', linewidth=1)

charts['emerging'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 13: Journal Landscape ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
top_journals = df['journal'].value_counts().head(15)
# Truncate very long journal names

    'font.family': 'sans-serif',

ACCENT = '#e74c3c'
BLUE1 = '#1b4f72'
BLUE2 = '#2e86c1'
GREEN1 = '#117a65'
ORANGE1 = '#d35400'

def fig_to_b64(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode()
    plt.close(fig)
    return f'data:image/png;base64,{b64}'

# ---------- Load Data ----------
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')
df['pub_date'] = pd.to_datetime(
    df['pub_year'].astype(str) + '-' + df['pub_month_num'].astype(str).replace('0', '01') + '-01',
    errors='coerce'
)

# Normalize countries
country_fix = {
    'United States': 'USA', 'United States of America': 'USA',
    'PR China': 'China', "People's Republic of China": 'China',
    'Republic of Korea': 'South Korea', 'P R China': 'China',
}
df['country_clean'] = df['country'].replace(country_fix)

# Parse research type
def get_primary_type(rt):
    if pd.isna(rt) or rt == '':
        return 'Other'
    types = [t.strip() for t in str(rt).split(';')]
    for t in ['Systematic Review', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Preprint',
              'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Editorial', 'Letter', 'Journal Article']:
        if t in types:
            return t
    return types[0] if types else 'Other'

df['primary_type'] = df['research_type'].apply(get_primary_type)

# Sort month-year
month_order = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec']
df['month_order'] = df['pub_month'].apply(lambda x: month_order.index(x) if x in month_order else 99)

charts = {}

# ==================== CHART 1: Monthly Publication Volume ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5.5))
monthly_data = []
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    for m_idx, m_name in enumerate(month_order):
        cnt = len(df[(df['pub_year'] == y) & (df['pub_month'] == m_name)])
        if cnt > 0 or not (y == 2026 and m_idx > 2):
            monthly_data.append({'label': f"{m_name}-{y}", 'year': y, 'month_idx': m_idx, 'count': cnt})

md = pd.DataFrame(monthly_data)

colors_by_year = {2024: BLUE1, 2025: BLUE2, 2026: GREEN1}
bar_colors = [colors_by_year.get(y, '#999') for y in md['year']]

bars = ax.bar(range(len(md)), md['count'], color=bar_colors, width=0.75, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)

# Add year separators
prev_year = None
for i, y in enumerate(md['year']):
    if y != prev_year:
        ax.axvline(x=i - 0.5, color='#ccc', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
        prev_year = y

ax.set_xticks(range(len(md)))
ax.set_xticklabels(md['label'], rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=7)
ax.set_ylabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Monthly Biomedical Publication Volume (Jan 2024 – Mar 2026)', fontweight='bold', pad=15)

legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=BLUE1, label='2024'),
                   Patch(facecolor=BLUE2, label='2025'),
                   Patch(facecolor=GREEN1, label='2026')]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(md['count']) * 1.15)

# Annotate peaks
top3 = md.nlargest(3, 'count')
for _, r in top3.iterrows():
    idx = md[md['label'] == r['label']].index[0]
    ax.annotate(f"{int(r['count'])}", (idx, r['count']), textcoords="offset points",
                xytext=(0, 6), ha='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=BLUE1)

# Add note about indexing skew

         fontsize=8, color='#999', ha='right')

ax.set_xticklabels(rt_oa_df['type'], rotation=30, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Open Access Rate by Research Type', fontweight='bold')
ax.axhline(y=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color=ORANGE1, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5,
           label=f'Overall ({df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%)')
ax.legend(fontsize=9)
for i, (v, c) in enumerate(zip(rt_oa_df['oa_rate'], rt_oa_df['count'])):
    ax.text(i, v + 1, f'{v:.1f}%\n(n={c})', ha='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')

charts['oa_research_type'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 12: Emerging Topics - Growth Rate ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.5))
# Calculate topics that appear in 2025/2026 but not heavily in 2024
topic_year_counts = df[df['major_topic'] != ''].groupby(['major_topic', 'pub_year']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
topic_year_counts = topic_year_counts[[2024, 2025, 2026]] if all(y in topic_year_counts.columns for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]) else topic_year_counts

# Growth topics: present in 2025/2026, with positive trajectory
topic_year_counts['growth_25_26'] = topic_year_counts[2026] - topic_year_counts[2025]
topic_year_counts['has_recent'] = (topic_year_counts[2025] > 0) | (topic_year_counts[2026] > 0)
topic_year_counts['increasing'] = topic_year_counts['growth_25_26'] > 0

emerging = topic_year_counts[topic_year_counts['has_recent']].sort_values('growth_25_26', ascending=False).head(15)
labels_em = [f"{t}\n(2024:{int(r[2024])} 2025:{int(r[2025])} 2026:{int(r[2026])})"
             for t, r in emerging.iterrows()]
vals_em = [r['growth_25_26'] for _, r in emerging.iterrows()]
colors_em = [GREEN1 if v > 0 else ORANGE1 for v in vals_em]

ax.barh(range(len(labels_em)-1, -1, -1), vals_em, color=colors_em[::-1], height=0.6, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(labels_em)-1, -1, -1))
ax.set_yticklabels(labels_em[::-1], fontsize=6.5)
ax.set_xlabel('Change in Publication Count (2026 – 2025)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Emerging Topics: Growth in Recent Publications (2025→2026)', fontweight='bold')
ax.axvline(x=0, color='#999', linewidth=1)

charts['emerging'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 13: Journal Landscape ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
top_journals = df['journal'].value_counts().head(15)
# Truncate very long journal names
short_names = []
for name in top_journals.index:
    if len(name) > 55:
        short_names.append(name[:52] + '...')
    else:
        short_names.append(name)

ax.barh(range(len(top_journals)-1, -1, -1), top_journals.values,
        color=[BLUE1 if i < 5 else BLUE2 if i < 10 else '#85c1e9' for i in range(len(top_journals))],
        height=0.7, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top_journals)-1, -1, -1))
ax.set_yticklabels(short_names[::-1], fontsize=7.5)
ax.set_xlabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Top 15 Journals by Publication Count', fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(top_journals.values[::-1]):
    ax.text(v + 0.3, i, str(v), va='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')

charts['journals'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 14: OA by Journal (Top) ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
top_j_oa = df['journal'].value_counts().head(15).index
j_oa_data = []
for j in top_j_oa:
    subset = df[df['journal'] == j]
    j_oa_data.append({'journal': j, 'oa_rate': subset['open_access'].mean() * 100, 'count': len(subset)})
j_oa_df = pd.DataFrame(j_oa_data).sort_values('oa_rate', ascending=True)

# Truncate names
j_short = []
for name in j_oa_df['journal']:
    j_short.append(name[:52] + '...' if len(name) > 55 else name)

colors_j_oa = [BLUE2 if r < 50 else GREEN1 if r > 75 else '#f9e79f' for r in j_oa_df['oa_rate']]
ax.barh(range(len(j_oa_df)), j_oa_df['oa_rate'], color=colors_j_oa, height=0.6, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(j_oa_df)))
ax.set_yticklabels(j_short, fontsize=7.5)
ax.set_xlabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Open Access Rate by Top Journals', fontweight='bold')
ax.axvline(x=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color=ORANGE1, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5,
           label=f'Overall ({df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%)')
ax.legend(fontsize=9)
for i, (v, c) in enumerate(zip(j_oa_df['oa_rate'], j_oa_df['count'])):
    ax.text(v + 0.5, i, f'{v:.0f}%', va='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')

charts['oa_journal'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== Save charts for report ====================
import json as _json
with open('/app/output/charts_metadata.json', 'w') as f:
    _json.dump(charts, f)

print("All charts generated successfully.")
print(f"Total charts: {len(charts)}")
for name in charts:
    print(f"  {name}: {len(charts[name])} chars")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the Biomedical Research Landscape 2024-2026 HTML report with embedded charts."""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
import seaborn as sns
from collections import Counter
import base64
import io
import json
from datetime import datetime

# ---------- Style ----------
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.labelsize': 12,
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'savefig.dpi': 150,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.1,
})

PALETTE = ['#1b4f72', '#2e86c1', '#3498db', '#85c1e9', '#d4e6f1',
           '#117a65', '#1abc9c', '#a3e4d7', '#d5f5e3', '#f9e79f',
           '#b03a2e', '#e74c3c', '#f1948a', '#fadbd8', '#7d3c98']
ACCENT = '#e74c3c'
BLUE1 = '#1b4f72'
BLUE2 = '#2e86c1'
GREEN1 = '#117a65'
ORANGE1 = '#d35400'

def fig_to_b64(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode()
    plt.close(fig)
    return f'data:image/png;base64,{b64}'

# ---------- Load Data ----------
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')
df['pub_date'] = pd.to_datetime(
    df['pub_year'].astype(str) + '-' + df['pub_month_num'].astype(str).replace('0', '01') + '-01',
    errors='coerce'
)

# Normalize countries
country_fix = {
    'United States': 'USA', 'United States of America': 'USA',
    'PR China': 'China', "People's Republic of China": 'China',
    'Republic of Korea': 'South Korea', 'P R China': 'China',
}
df['country_clean'] = df['country'].replace(country_fix)

# Parse research type
def get_primary_type(rt):
    if pd.isna(rt) or rt == '':
        return 'Other'
    types = [t.strip() for t in str(rt).split(';')]
    for t in ['Systematic Review', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Preprint',
              'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Editorial', 'Letter', 'Journal Article']:
        if t in types:
            return t
    return types[0] if types else 'Other'

df['primary_type'] = df['research_type'].apply(get_primary_type)

# Sort month-year
month_order = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec']
df['month_order'] = df['pub_month'].apply(lambda x: month_order.index(x) if x in month_order else 99)

charts = {}

# ==================== CHART 1: Monthly Publication Volume ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5.5))
monthly_data = []
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    for m_idx, m_name in enumerate(month_order):
        cnt = len(df[(df['pub_year'] == y) & (df['pub_month'] == m_name)])
        if cnt > 0 or not (y == 2026 and m_idx > 2):
            monthly_data.append({'label': f"{m_name}-{y}", 'year': y, 'month_idx': m_idx, 'count': cnt})

md = pd.DataFrame(monthly_data)

colors_by_year = {2024: BLUE1, 2025: BLUE2, 2026: GREEN1}
bar_colors = [colors_by_year.get(y, '#999') for y in md['year']]

bars = ax.bar(range(len(md)), md['count'], color=bar_colors, width=0.75, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)

# Add year separators
prev_year = None
for i, y in enumerate(md['year']):
    if y != prev_year:
        ax.axvline(x=i - 0.5, color='#ccc', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
        prev_year = y

ax.set_xticks(range(len(md)))
ax.set_xticklabels(md['label'], rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=7)
ax.set_ylabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Monthly Biomedical Publication Volume (Jan 2024 – Mar 2026)', fontweight='bold', pad=15)

from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=BLUE1, label='2024'),
                   Patch(facecolor=BLUE2, label='2025'),
                   Patch(facecolor=GREEN1, label='2026')]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(md['count']) * 1.15)

# Annotate peaks
top3 = md.nlargest(3, 'count')
for _, r in top3.iterrows():
    idx = md[md['label'] == r['label']].index[0]
    ax.annotate(f"{int(r['count'])}", (idx, r['count']), textcoords="offset points",
                xytext=(0, 6), ha='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=BLUE1)

# Add note about indexing skew
ax.text(0.99, 0.95, 'Note: 2024 dominance reflects PubMed indexing lag;\n2025-2026 records still accumulating.',
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8, ha='right', va='top',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='#fff3cd', alpha=0.8))

charts['monthly_volume'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 2: Yearly Volume + OA ====================
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.5))

# Yearly volume
yearly = df.groupby('pub_year').size()
years = [2024, 2025, 2026]
counts = [yearly.get(y, 0) for y in years]
colors_yr = [BLUE1, BLUE2, GREEN1]
bars = ax1.bar(years, counts, color=colors_yr, width=0.6, edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)
for bar, c in zip(bars, counts):
    ax1.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 30, f'{c:,}',
             ha='center', fontweight='bold', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_ylabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Total Publications by Year', fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xticks(years)

# OA rate over time
oa_yearly = df.groupby('pub_year')['open_access'].mean() * 100
oa_rates = [oa_yearly.get(y, 0) for y in years]
ax2.plot(years, oa_rates, 'o-', color=ORANGE1, linewidth=2.5, markersize=10, markerfacecolor='white',
         markeredgewidth=2)
for y, r in zip(years, oa_rates):
    ax2.annotate(f'{r:.1f}%', (y, r), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 12),
                 ha='center', fontweight='bold', fontsize=11, color=ORANGE1)
ax2.set_ylabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold', color=ORANGE1)
ax2.set_title('Open Access Rate by Year', fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xticks(years)
ax2.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax2.axhline(y=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color='#999', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.6)
ax2.text(2025.5, df['open_access'].mean() * 100 + 1, f'Overall: {df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%',
         fontsize=8, color='#999', ha='right')

fig.tight_layout()
charts['yearly_oa'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 3: OA Monthly Trend ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
df_km = df[df['pub_month_num'] != 0].copy()
df_km['ym_label'] = df_km['pub_month'].astype(str) + '-' + df_km['pub_year'].astype(str)
oa_monthly = df_km.groupby('ym_label')['open_access'].agg(['mean', 'count']).reset_index()
oa_monthly['mean'] = oa_monthly['mean'] * 100

# Sort
monthly_labels = []
for y in [2024, 2025, 2026]:
    for m in month_order:
        label = f"{m}-{y}"
        if label in oa_monthly['ym_label'].values:
            monthly_labels.append(label)

oa_monthly['sort_key'] = oa_monthly['ym_label'].apply(
    lambda x: monthly_labels.index(x) if x in monthly_labels else 999)
oa_monthly = oa_monthly.sort_values('sort_key')

# Color by year
bar_colors = []
for _, r in oa_monthly.iterrows():
    yr = int(r['ym_label'].split('-')[1])
    bar_colors.append({2024: BLUE1, 2025: BLUE2, 2026: GREEN1}.get(yr, '#999'))

ax.bar(range(len(oa_monthly)), oa_monthly['mean'], color=bar_colors, width=0.7, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)
ax.axhline(y=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color=ORANGE1, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.7,
           label=f'Overall ({df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%)')
ax.set_xticks(range(len(oa_monthly)))
ax.set_xticklabels(oa_monthly['ym_label'], rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=7)
ax.set_ylabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Monthly Open Access Rate', fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(loc='lower left', fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylim(0, 105)

# Add trend line
xs = range(len(oa_monthly))
z = np.polyfit(xs, oa_monthly['mean'].values, 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)
ax.plot(xs, p(xs), color=ORANGE1, linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.5, linestyle='-')

charts['oa_monthly'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 4: Geographic Distribution ====================
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5.5))

top15 = df['country_clean'].value_counts().head(15)
colors_geo = [BLUE1 if i < 5 else BLUE2 if i < 10 else '#85c1e9' for i in range(len(top15))]
ax1.barh(range(len(top15)-1, -1, -1), top15.values, color=colors_geo[::-1], height=0.7, edgecolor='white')
ax1.set_yticks(range(len(top15)-1, -1, -1))
ax1.set_yticklabels(top15.index[::-1], fontsize=9)
ax1.set_xlabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Top 15 Countries by Publication Count', fontweight='bold')
for i, (val, name) in enumerate(zip(top15.values[::-1], top15.index[::-1])):
    ax1.text(val + 3, i, str(val), va='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=BLUE1)

# Top 5 country share over time
top5_countries = ['China', 'USA', 'India', 'Japan', 'Canada']
year_country_data = {}
for y in years:
    y_df = df[df['pub_year'] == y]
    total = len(y_df)
    year_country_data[y] = {}
    for c in top5_countries:
        year_country_data[y][c] = len(y_df[y_df['country_clean'] == c]) / total * 100

x = np.arange(len(years))
width = 0.15
for i, country in enumerate(top5_countries):
    vals = [year_country_data[y].get(country, 0) for y in years]
    ax2.bar(x + i * width, vals, width, label=country, color=PALETTE[i], edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)

ax2.set_ylabel('Share of Publications (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Top 5 Countries: Share Over Time', fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xticks(x + width * 2)
ax2.set_xticklabels(years)
ax2.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)

fig.tight_layout()
charts['geography'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 5: OA by Country ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
top12 = df['country_clean'].value_counts().head(12).index
oa_by_country = []
for c in top12:
    subset = df[df['country_clean'] == c]
    oa_by_country.append({'country': c, 'oa_rate': subset['open_access'].mean() * 100, 'count': len(subset)})
oa_df = pd.DataFrame(oa_by_country).sort_values('oa_rate', ascending=True)

colors_oa_cty = [BLUE2 if r < df['open_access'].mean() * 100 else GREEN1 for r in oa_df['oa_rate']]
ax.barh(range(len(oa_df)), oa_df['oa_rate'], color=colors_oa_cty, height=0.6, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(oa_df)))
ax.set_yticklabels(oa_df['country'], fontsize=10)
ax.set_xlabel('Open Access Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Open Access Rate by Top Countries', fontweight='bold')
ax.axvline(x=df['open_access'].mean() * 100, color=ORANGE1, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5,
           label=f'Overall ({df["open_access"].mean()*100:.1f}%)')
ax.legend(loc='lower right', fontsize=9)
for i, (val, cnt) in enumerate(zip(oa_df['oa_rate'], oa_df['count'])):
    ax.text(val + 0.5, i, f'{val:.1f}% (n={cnt})', va='center', fontsize=8, color='#333')

charts['oa_country'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 6: Major Topics ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
top_topics = df[df['major_topic'] != '']['major_topic'].value_counts().head(20)
colors_topic = [BLUE1 if i < 5 else BLUE2 if i < 10 else '#85c1e9' for i in range(len(top_topics))]
ax.barh(range(len(top_topics)-1, -1, -1), top_topics.values, color=colors_topic[::-1], height=0.7, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top_topics)-1, -1, -1))
ax.set_yticklabels(top_topics.index[::-1], fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Top 20 Major MeSH Topics', fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(top_topics.values[::-1]):
    ax.text(v + 0.2, i, str(v), va='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=BLUE1)

charts['topics'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 7: Topic Trends ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
# Focus on top topics that appear across years
trend_topics = ['COVID-19', 'Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2', 'Breast Neoplasms',
                'Gastrointestinal Microbiome', 'Alzheimer Disease', 'MicroRNAs',
                'Quality of Life', 'Neoplasms']
trend_data = []
for topic in trend_topics:
    for y in years:
        cnt = len(df[(df['pub_year'] == y) & (df['major_topic'] == topic)])
        trend_data.append({'topic': topic, 'year': y, 'count': cnt})
td = pd.DataFrame(trend_data)

for i, topic in enumerate(trend_topics):
    t_sub = td[td['topic'] == topic]
    ax.plot(t_sub['year'], t_sub['count'], 'o-', color=PALETTE[i], linewidth=2, markersize=6, label=topic)

ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Publications', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Major Topic Publication Trends (2024–2026)', fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2, loc='upper right')
ax.set_xticks(years)

charts['topic_trends'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 8: Keywords Word Cloud Alternative (Top Keywords) ====================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
# Get top keywords excluding generic ones
generic_kw = {'Humans', 'Female', 'Male', 'Animals', 'Adult', 'Middle Aged', 'Aged', 'nan',
              'Child', 'Adolescent', 'Young Adult', 'Child, Preschool', 'Infant', 'Infant, Newborn'}
all_kw = []
for kw in df[df['keywords'] != '']['keywords']:
    all_kw.extend([k.strip() for k in str(kw).split(';')])
kw_counter = Counter(all_kw)
top_kw_disease = [(kw, cnt) for kw, cnt in kw_counter.most_common(100) if kw not in generic_kw][:25]

labels_kw = [k for k, _ in top_kw_disease]
values_kw = [v for _, v in top_kw_disease]
colors_kw = [BLUE1 if i < 8 else BLUE2 if i < 16 else '#85c1e9' for i in range(len(labels_kw))]

ax.barh(range(len(labels_kw)-1, -1, -1), values_kw, color=colors_kw[::-1], height=0.7, edgecolor='white')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(labels_kw)-1, -1, -1))
ax.set_yticklabels(labels_kw[::-1], fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel('Occurrences', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Top 25 Domain-Specific MeSH Keywords (Excluding Demographics)', fontweight='bold')

charts['keywords'] = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ==================== CHART 9: Research Type Distribution ====================
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5))

rt_counts = df['primary_type'].value_counts()
explode = [0.03 if c == 'Journal Article' else 0 for c in rt_counts.index]
colors_rt = [BLUE1, BLUE2, GREEN1, '#85c1e9', ORANGE1, '#a3e4d7', '#d5f5e3', '#f9e79f', '#f1948a']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax1.pie(rt_counts.values, labels=rt_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%',
                                    colors=colors_rt[:len(rt_counts)], startangle=140,
                                    textprops={'fontsize': 8}, pctdistance=0.75)
for at in autotexts:
    at.set_fontweight('bold')
ax1.set_title('Research Type Distribution', fontweight='bold')

# Authors by research type
rt_order = ['Journal Article', 'Review', 'Case Reports', 'Systematic Review',
            'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Preprint']
rt_meds = []
for rt in rt_order:
    subset = df[df['primary_type'] == rt]
    if len(subset) > 0:
        rt_meds.append({'type': rt, 'median': subset['authors_count'].median(), 'count': len(subset)})
rt_meds_df = pd.DataFrame(rt_meds)
ax2.barh(range(len(rt_meds_df)-1, -1, -1), rt_meds_df['median'],
         color=[BLUE1, BLUE2, GREEN1, '#85c1e9', ORANGE1, '#a3e4d7'][:len(rt_meds_df)],
         height=0.6, edgecolor='white')
ax2.set_yticks(range(len(rt_meds_df)-1, -1, -1))
ax2.set_yticklabels(rt_meds_df['type'][::-1], fontsize=9)
ax2.set_xlabel('Median Authors', fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Median Authors per Research Type', fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(rt_meds_df['median'][::-1]):

steps.message:
The report has been generated at **`/app/output/final_report.html`** (1.6 MB, self-contained, opens directly in any browser).

**Report structure:**

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Hero + KPI Dashboard | 5 metric cards (4,886 publications, 65.1% OA, 6 median authors, 52.9% top-10 share, 2,055 journals) |
| 1. Publication Volume & Trends | Monthly bar chart (Jan 2024–Mar 2026), yearly breakdown table, seasonality analysis, indexing-lag caveat |
| 2. Geographic Landscape | Top 15 countries horizontal bar chart, top-5 country share over time (grouped bars), OA rate by top-12 countries |
| 3. Topic & MeSH Analysis | Top 20 major topics, topic trends over time (8 key topics), top 25 domain-specific keywords, emerging topics growth chart |
| 4. Open Access & Journals | Monthly OA rate trend with regression line, OA by research type, top 15 journals, OA by journal with overall benchmark |
| 5. Research Type & Collaboration | Pie chart + median authors by type, author count histogram, median authors by top-10 countries |
| 6. Key Takeaways | 7 prioritized strategic insights (3 priority levels) with a bottom-line executive summary |
| Appendix | Data sources, methodology, normalization rules, limitations |

**13 embedded charts** (base64 PNGs) covering all specified KPIs: total publications by year, OA rate over time, median authors, top-10 country share, and emerging topic growth rate.
